name: velocity rounds a tie up even where a float misses it
about: velocity at 0.7 is 700 thousandths, so a product that is exactly a half rounds away from zero, including the two a double computes just below the half.
notes: out = clamp(floor((v * 700 + 500) / 1000), 1, 127), on a note on with v > 0. That is round to nearest, ties away from zero, of v * 0.7 done exactly.
t 1: v 85 (55). 85 * 700 = 59500, + 500 = 60000, / 1000 = 60 = 3C. A TIE that a double also misses: Math.round(85 * 0.7) is 59.
t 2: v 5 (05). 3500 + 500 = 4000, / 1000 = 4 = 04. A tie a double gets right, here so the rule is not only graded where floats fail.
NEGATIVE CONTROL t 6: a note off 80 3C 2D passes unchanged. Scaled it would read 80 3C 20.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: l2 asks for scale 0.0004, which is 0.4 thousandths and rounds to 0, so it is refused bad-args, in both languages.
